title: pdl-lint reports a schema error as a list repr
notes: The `PDLParseError: ` prefix is gone: `e.text` is already a rendered diagnostic with its own header, and putting PDL's internal class name in front of it was the interpreter's vocabulary leaking into the linter -- `pdl` prints this same diagnostic without it, so the two tools now spell one error the same way. The diagnostic is now indented as a block to the linter's five-space gutter (`_indent_diagnostic`), so the second line of one error lines up with its first. This was recorded against E-LINT-001, -002 and -003 as a shared unfixed defect and was briefly mistaken for the group's convention; it was not one, and the entry notes that penalised it were right. The block is shifted, never re-wrapped: the continuation lines are the rendered text's own structure and are positioned relative to each other by `pdl_diagnostics.render` and `pdl_interpreter._wrap`, which are also what a reader sees when the same diagnostic reaches them from `pdl`. Blank lines stay blank rather than becoming five spaces of trailing whitespace. Measured cost: the widest *body* line grows by five, reaching 82 columns here and 81 in E-LINT-003 -- inside the envelope the tool already had, since E-LINT-002's header is 89 columns and is unchanged. Hygiene 2 -> 3: both defects previously recorded here are gone and nothing else is leaking. Location/what/why/fix do not move, and that is the point of the entry: its `fix: 0` and `why: 1` are E-SCHEMA-001's gaps displayed through the linter, not linter defects. There is no "did you mean `parameters`?" because the interpreter has none; landing the schema suggestion once will move this entry and E-SCHEMA-002 together, and a linter-local patch would duplicate logic that belongs one layer down. Correcting a stale clause in the previous note: there *is* a column -- the golden reads `prog.pdl:5:5`, the `:col` work having landed after that sentence was written. Still no excerpt and no caret, which is what holds location at 2. **Fix 0 -> 3, and it arrived exactly as this note predicted it would.** The `did you mean `parameters:` instead of `parameterss:`?` line is the interpreter's, landed once in `pdl_schema_error_analyzer`; the linter prints `e.text` and gained it without a line of linter-side change, which is what makes a second, linter-local near miss the wrong shape. `_indent_diagnostic` shifts the new `help:` line to the five-space gutter with the rest of the block and leaves the blank line above it blank, so the widest body line is unchanged at 82 columns and the entry's Hygiene 3 is undisturbed. Why stays 1 for the same reason it does in E-SCHEMA-001: the diagnostic still names no valid alternative.
